list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites.

list.name: cidr
list.label: CIDR filter
list.description: Restrict the graph to links with an endpoint in this range (or both endpoints -- see Scope), e.g. 10.12.0.0/16, 10.12.6.0/24, or a bare IP. Leave empty for no filter. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round down to the enclosing octet boundary, so /20 behaves as /16 and may show a wider range than typed.

list.name: scope
list.label: Scope
list.description: either: every link touching the CIDR range, so its outside peers are drawn too. both: only links with both ends inside the range -- the internal topology of a subnet. Has no effect while the CIDR box is empty.
list.query: either endpoint in range : either,both endpoints in range : both

list.name: links
list.label: Links drawn
list.description: How many of the busiest links (by bytes) to draw. Nodes are the endpoints of those links. Past a few hundred the layout becomes a hairball and the browser slows down; narrow with the CIDR box instead of raising this.

panels.title: Topology -- busiest $links links
panels.description: One node per host, one arrow per (initiator -> responder) pair, drawn for the busiest links in range. Node: total bytes on the drawn links, and how many of them it has. The ring splits those bytes by role -- blue for connections the host opened, green for connections it answered -- so a server is mostly green and a workstation mostly blue. Edge thickness is log-scaled bytes. A public address is labelled with its country ("public · DE"), from the GeoIP tags the collector writes; flows recorded before it had a GeoIP database carry none, so those read just "public". Click a node for its menu (host drilldown, country). IP geolocation by DB-IP (db-ip.com).

targets.query:
import "array"
import "dict"
import "math"
import "regexp"
import "strings"

// Same helper as the traffic dashboards: the CIDR box becomes an anchored prefix
// regex, the only form InfluxDB pushes down to storage. Prefix lengths other
// than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round DOWN to the enclosing octet boundary, so the
// range can be wider than typed -- never narrower.
cidrPrefix = (cidr) => {
    p = strings.split(v: cidr, t: "/")
    bits = if length(arr: p) > 1 then int(v: p[1]) else 32
    o = strings.split(v: p[0], t: ".")

    return
        if bits <= 8 then "^" + o[0] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 16 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\."
        else if bits <= 24 then "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\."
        else "^" + o[0] + "\\." + o[1] + "\\." + o[2] + "\\." + o[3] + "$"
}

cidrRe = if "${cidr}" == "" then /.*/ else regexp.compile(v: cidrPrefix(cidr: "${cidr}"))

// "both" narrows to links that stay inside the range. It is a second regex
// filter rather than a conditional inside one, because a conditional does not
// push down and two chained tag regexes do.
bothRe = if "${scope}" == "both" then cidrRe else /.*/

// A link is a (src_ip, dst_ip) pair. nfstream flows are bidirectional with the
// initiator as src, so the arrow means "opened connections to", and the bytes
// are both directions. Only the busiest ${links} links are drawn: the node graph
// is unreadable long before Grafana's own limits, and the production mirror has
// ~3.5k hosts.
links = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ cidrRe or r.dst_ip =~ cidrRe)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ bothRe and r.dst_ip =~ bothRe)
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "dst_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: ${links})
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: float(v: r._value)}))

// Country of every drawn endpoint, from the collector's src_country/dst_country
// tags. Only the (at most 2 x ${links}) addresses actually drawn are looked up:
// they become one anchored regex, which pushes down like the CIDR one, and
// group + last() per address pushes down too -- so this reads the last block
// of a few series, not the range again. Flows written before the collector had
// a GeoIP database carry no tag, so a host seen only then has no country.
drawn = union(tables: [
    links |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with ip: r.src_ip})),
    links |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with ip: r.dst_ip})),
  ])
  |> keep(columns: ["ip"])
  |> group()
  |> unique(column: "ip")
  |> findColumn(fn: (key) => true, column: "ip")
drawnRe = regexp.compile(v: "^(" + strings.joinStr(arr: array.map(arr: drawn, fn: (x) => regexp.quoteMeta(v: x)), v: "|") + ")$")
ccFlows = () => from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
ccPairs = union(tables: [
    ccFlows()
      |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dst_ip =~ drawnRe and r.dst_country =~ /^[A-Z]{2}$/)
      |> group(columns: ["dst_ip", "dst_country"])
      |> last()
      |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with kv: r.dst_ip + "=" + r.dst_country})),
    ccFlows()
      |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip =~ drawnRe and r.src_country =~ /^[A-Z]{2}$/)
      |> group(columns: ["src_ip", "src_country"])
      |> last()
      |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with kv: r.src_ip + "=" + r.src_country})),
  ])
  |> keep(columns: ["kv"])
  |> group()
  |> unique(column: "kv")
  |> findColumn(fn: (key) => true, column: "kv")
countries = dict.fromList(pairs: array.map(arr: ccPairs, fn: (x) => {
    p = strings.split(v: x, t: "=")
    return {key: p[0], value: p[1]}
}))

// The node graph prints a number as toFixed(2) plus its unit taken literally
// ("9948.00 bytes"), whatever the field config or panel options say, and passes
// strings through untouched -- so the stats are formatted here, in the same
// binary units the table uses.
human = (b) =>
  if b >= 1073741824.0 then string(v: math.round(x: b / 107374182.4) / 10.0) + " GiB"
  else if b >= 1048576.0 then string(v: math.round(x: b / 104857.6) / 10.0) + " MiB"
  else if b >= 1024.0 then string(v: math.round(x: b / 102.4) / 10.0) + " KiB"
  else string(v: int(v: b)) + " B"

// Edges: the node graph recognises this frame by its source/target fields.
// Thickness is log-scaled -- 10 kB is 1px, 1 GB and up is 8px -- because
// byte counts here span seven orders of magnitude.
links
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with
      id: r.src_ip + " > " + r.dst_ip,
      source: r.src_ip,
      target: r.dst_ip,
      mainstat: human(b: r._value),
      thickness: math.mMax(x: 1.0, y: math.mMin(x: 8.0, y: math.log10(x: r._value) - 3.0))}))
  |> keep(columns: ["id", "source", "target", "mainstat", "thickness"])
  |> yield(name: "edges")

// Nodes are derived from the drawn links, not read again, so every edge has
// both of its ends and no node is left floating. map/reduce are fine here: they
// run on at most two rows per link, after the pushdown aggregate.
union(tables: [
    links |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with id: r.src_ip, client: r._value, server: 0.0})),
    links |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with id: r.dst_ip, client: 0.0, server: r._value})),
  ])
  |> keep(columns: ["id", "client", "server"])
  |> group(columns: ["id"])
  |> reduce(
      identity: {client: 0.0, server: 0.0, links: 0},
      fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
        client: accumulator.client + r.client,
        server: accumulator.server + r.server,
        links: accumulator.links + 1}))
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with
      title: r.id,
      subtitle:
        if strings.containsStr(v: r.id, substr: ":") then "IPv6"
        else if r.id == "0.0.0.0" then "unspecified"
        else if r.id =~ /^(22[4-9]|23[0-9])\./ then "multicast"
        else if r.id =~ /^255\./ or r.id =~ /\.255$/ then "broadcast"
        else if r.id =~ /^(10\.|192\.168\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.)/
          then regexp.replaceAllString(r: /\.[0-9]+$/, v: r.id, t: ".0/24")
        else if dict.get(dict: countries, key: r.id, default: "") != ""
          then "public · " + dict.get(dict: countries, key: r.id, default: "")
        else "public",
      detail__country: dict.get(dict: countries, key: r.id, default: ""),
      mainstat: human(b: r.client + r.server),
      secondarystat: string(v: r.links) + (if r.links == 1 then " link" else " links"),
      arc__client: r.client / (r.client + r.server),
      arc__server: r.server / (r.client + r.server)}))
  |> keep(columns: ["id", "title", "subtitle", "mainstat", "secondarystat", "detail__country", "arc__client", "arc__server"])
  |> yield(name: "nodes")

panels.title: Drawn Links
panels.description: The links the graph draws, as a table: the same query, so the two always agree. Click an address to open its host drilldown. Country is the endpoint's GeoIP country (public addresses only).
